canonical_name: Instanton Floer homology as a three-manifold invariant
canonical_statement: Provisional exact-scope reading: for every closed oriented integral homology 3-sphere Y, its instanton Floer homology, constructed from the SU(2) instanton/Floer complex with conventions fixed by the statement phase, is well-defined up to the selected equivalence and is invariant under orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of Y.
domain_and_universes: A Lean encoding of closed oriented smooth 3-manifolds satisfying the integral-homology-sphere condition, SU(2) bundles/connections and gauge equivalence, the instanton Floer chain complex, a relative Z/8 grading, and homology in a fixed coefficient category. Universes and concrete structures remain unselected.
quantifiers: for every closed oriented integral homology 3-sphere Y
for every pair of admissible auxiliary choices used to construct the instanton Floer complex of Y
for every orientation-preserving diffeomorphism f : Y -> Y' between objects in the selected domain
hypotheses: Y and Y' satisfy the closed, oriented, smooth, three-dimensional, integral-homology-sphere conditions selected at the statement gate
the gauge group, bundle, perturbation, transversality, compactness, orientation, grading, and coefficient conventions are those fixed by the canonical construction
f is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism when the invariance clause is applied
conclusion: The resulting graded homology object is independent, in the precisely selected sense, of the allowed auxiliary choices, and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism induces the selected isomorphism/equivalence of instanton Floer homology objects.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: whether the root is restricted to oriented integral homology 3-spheres exactly as in the 1988 construction or uses a later admissible-bundle variant
the gauge group and bundle data and the treatment or exclusion of reducible connections
the coefficient ring and relative grading convention
whether well-definedness means noncanonical graded isomorphism, canonical isomorphism, chain-homotopy equivalence, or functoriality
whether the credited invariance is only orientation-preserving diffeomorphism invariance and how orientation reversal acts
which analytic construction hypotheses belong in the root rather than in proof architecture
excluded_degenerate_cases: The repository phrase does not justify a claim for every topological 3-manifold, manifolds with boundary, nonorientable manifolds, or arbitrary homology. A numerical invariant, Euler characteristic alone, the Casson invariant relation, a later instanton variant, or invariance of only a chain presentation is not a substitute for the selected homology-object claim. Orientation-reversing maps are outside the provisional root until audited.
